parts.article:
The unsung sense
 
New research reassesses the nature and importance of smell
 
(A) Traditionally, smell has not been at the forefront of sensory research, pushed aside in favour of the seemingly more vital senses of vision and hearing. There has been a strong belief that people, especially compared to other mammals, are not that influenced by smells.
 
(B) One of the first to assert the relative unimportance of the human sense of smell was Pierre Paul Broca, an influential 19th-century anatomist. After comparing the proportion of the brain devoted to smell in different animals, he suggested that mammals can be classed into two broad groups: macrosmatic mammals, such as dogs, have a finely tuned sense of smell which they rely on to perceive the world, while marine mammals and primates, including humans, are microsmatic – the organ with which they smell is small and functionally redundant.
 
(C) That idea seemed to fit with more recent studies in genetics, which found that the majority of mammals have about one thousand different types of smell receptor. Most of these aren't present in humans, who only possess four hundred or so different types.
 
(D) Yet these findings may have been misleading. Brain scans show that more of the human brain is devoted to smell processing than Broca's anatomical studies suggested. And although we may have fewer types of receptor than other mammals, research has shown that the human nose and brain are unusually well connected, with each group of receptors linking to many more neural regions than is the case in other animals. That should give us a good ability to process incoming scents.
 
(E) Once researchers began looking, they found the nose to be far more sensitive than its reputation suggested. One study, for example, found that we can pick out a particular substance even when heavily diluted. In fact, a person can smell just one drop of a chemical in a large swimming pool.
 
(F) What's more, with the latest findings, it is becoming clear that the brain's smelling centres are intimately linked to its system for controlling emotion, fear and memory. That suggests a link between smell and the way we think. One Dutch academic, for example, found that when the smell of orange, seawater or peppermint was pumped through a nightclub, those inside partied harder – they danced more, laughed more, and even thought the music was better than when there was no added scent.
 
(G) Other work has found that scent can influence our cognitive skills. A study found that when men were subjected to a novel smell – either good or bad – during a task used to test decision-making skills, they performed significantly worse than normal. The researchers concluded that the scent stimulated brain areas connected with emotion, making their decisions emotional rather than rational.
 
(H) The surprising thing about such studies is that up to 95% of subjects altered their behaviour, despite only 5% of them being aware of the introduced smells that they were facing. The question, then, is why do we pay so little conscious attention to our noses unless we smell something really strong?
 
(I) One vital factor is that our noses just aren't equipped to locate the source of an odour. This makes the sense of smell fundamentally different to vision or hearing, which are built to identify sights and sounds with precision. Apparently, we become aware of something when the brain focuses on a single location, after which it picks out the details, like a familiar face, from the scene. With smell, though, the brain does not focus in the same way, and so is not able to make us aware of the details relating to one particular area. It's for this reason that we can only ever pick out around four smells from a complex mixture.
 
(J) Nevertheless, we all have the capacity to train our sense of smell, but it needs to be worked at. Master perfumers, for instance, learn to recognise, name and imagine an extraordinary range of smells through years of practice. This is accompanied by a significant reorganisation of the olfactory areas in the brain that helps them to process the scents more efficiently.
 
(K) Smells are also especially good memory evokers, but it's actually a myth that odours trigger more complete memories than other stimuli. These memories are neither more accurate nor more detailed, but they are unique in that they are more emotional. This isn't surprising when you consider that both emotion and smell are processed by the same areas of the brain, and there is a strong link between emotion and memory.
 
(L) That said, not all smell memories are equal. The link between a memory and a smell is stronger if the smell is an unpleasant rather than a pleasant one, which makes sense from an evolutionary perspective. In addition, the very first time we associate a smell with an object, it evokes a much greater response in our brains than for any encounter with the smell or object in later life, laying down stronger foundations for the memory. That doesn't happen with any other sense. Since most first encounters with a smell happen at a young age, this might explain why smells often carry us back to our childhood.

reference:
Q1

干扰 题目中已经有了“humans”，所以填空处不能再填humans，要填与其并列的“primates”。

句子 （B段）： ...while marine mammals and primates, including humans, are microsmatic – the organ with which they smell is small and functionally redundant.

解析 定位到B段，Broca将哺乳动物分为两类，人类与“primates（灵长类动物）”和海洋哺乳动物被归为第二类（microsmatic），即嗅觉器官较小的一类。

Q2

解析 定位到C段，文中明确对比：大多数哺乳动物有约1000种受体，而人类只有“four hundred（400）”种左右。

干扰 一定要看清主语是“humans”，不要填成其他哺乳动物的数字“one thousand”。

句子 （C段）： Most of these aren't present in humans, who only possess four hundred or so different types.

Q3

解析 定位到E段，文中说人可以在大游泳池里闻出“just one drop（仅仅一滴）”的化学物质。

干扰 题目中的“a single”对应文中的“one”，后面紧跟的量词就是答案，不要填成“chemical”。

句子 （E段）： In fact, a person can smell just one drop of a chemical in a large swimming pool.

Q4

干扰 题目问的是地点（into a ...），文中对应“pumped through a nightclub”。

解析 定位到F段，一位荷兰学者将气味泵入一家“nightclub（夜店）”来进行研究。

句子 （F段）： One Dutch academic, for example, found that when the smell of orange, seawater or peppermint was pumped through a nightclub, those inside partied harder...

Q5

解析 继续在F段，研究发现里面的人觉得“music（音乐）”比没有香味时听起来更好。

干扰 题目问的是“felt about（对...的感觉）”，文中对应“thought the music was better”。

句子 （F段）： ...they danced more, laughed more, and even thought the music was better than when there was no added scent.

Q6

解析 定位到H段，文中提到高达“95%”的受试者改变了行为（reacted）。

干扰 千万别填“5%”，那是“意识到（aware）”有气味的人数比例，题目问的是“有反应（reacted/altered behaviour）”的人。

句子 （H段）： The surprising thing about such studies is that up to 95% of subjects altered their behaviour, despite only 5% of them being aware of the introduced smells that they were facing.

Q7

句子 （I段）： This makes the sense of smell fundamentally different to vision or hearing, which are built to identify sights and sounds with precision.

干扰 题目中的“locate exactly”对应文中的“identify... with precision”。

解析 文章I段明确说，嗅觉无法定位来源，这使得它与视觉听觉有着本质不同，后者是“built to identify sights and sounds with precision（生来就是为了精确识别图像和声音位置的）”。

Q8

解析 文章I段末尾提到，在复杂的混合气味中，我们只能挑出“around four（大约四种）”气味。

干扰 题目中的“only a few”对应文中的“around four”，“complex multiple smells”对应文中的“complex mixture”。

句子 （I段）： It's for this reason that we can only ever pick out around four smells from a complex mixture.

Q9

解析 文章J段虽然提到嗅觉可以通过训练提升，并举了调香大师（Master perfumers）作为例子，但从未说普通人训练时“is needed（必须有）”专业帮助。

干扰 不要看到“Master perfumers”就觉得一定要拜师学艺，文中说的是“needs to be worked at（需要努力/练习）”，不是需要老师。

句子 （J段）： Nevertheless, we all have the capacity to train our sense of smell, but it needs to be worked at. Master perfumers, for instance, learn to recognise...

Q10

句子 （K段）： ...but it's actually a myth that odours trigger more complete memories than other stimuli. These memories are neither more accurate nor more detailed...

解析 文章K段直接指出，认为气味能触发更完整的记忆是一个“myth（迷思/误区）”，这些记忆并不比其他感官的记忆“more accurate nor more detailed（更准确或更细节）”。

干扰 题目中的“more precise（更精确）”与文中的“neither more accurate nor more detailed”直接矛盾。

Q11

解析 文章L段开头明确说，如果气味是“unpleasant rather than a pleasant one（难闻的而不是好闻的）”，记忆的连接会“stronger（更强）”。

干扰 注意比较级，文中说是“unpleasant”更强，题目说“pleasant”最强，二者矛盾。

句子 （L段）： The link between a memory and a smell is stronger if the smell is an unpleasant rather than a pleasant one, which makes sense from an evolutionary perspective.

Q12

解析 文章L段虽然解释了为什么成年后遇到的新气味激发的反应不如第一次（通常在童年）强烈，但并没有说人的“Sensitivity（生理敏感度）”在下降。

干扰 “第一次遇到反应大”不等于“成年后嗅觉退化”，不要把“大脑反应机制”和“感官灵敏度”混淆。（L段）： （L段讨论的是第一次遇到气味时的记忆深度，而非生理上的嗅觉敏感度是否随年龄下降。）

句子 （L段）： （L段讨论的是第一次遇到气味时的记忆深度，而非生理上的嗅觉敏感度是否随年龄下降。）

Q13

解析 文章L段最后一句总结道，因为大多数气味的第一次接触都发生在年轻时，这就解释了为什么气味“often carry us back to our childhood（经常把我们带回童年）”。

干扰 题目中的“frequently”对应文中的“often”。

句子 （L段）： Since most first encounters with a smell happen at a young age, this might explain why smells often carry us back to our childhood.
